Receiving his A.B. degree in 1883, he was given a position as teacher of English and German in the College in addition to some preparatory subjects and was retained the next year to teach natural science. He told that he was Senior assistant editor of one of the paper's early issues and was Business Manager later in the year.

The following account of Mr. Pierce's service after he left Savoy College (in 1887) is quoted through the courtesy of Mrs. Pierce:

Leonidas William Pierce . . . attended the Southern Baptist Theological Seminary at Louisville, Kentucky, finishing the course in 1892. He and a party of young volunteers who were sent by the Foreign Board of the Southern Baptist Convention as missionaries to Yangchow, China.

For months after his arrival in China, he and Miss Molly E. Tupper of the mission were married in 1893. He spent his entire missionary career with the missionaries in Yanochow, a city, at that time, of about four hundred thousand people and whose inhabitants did not know whether they wanted the Saviour who saves for eternity, or of the God who had saved them.

The first few years were very difficult years. The Chinese language was not easy to learn. It was in fact a discouraging undertaking. Mr. Pierce, though he has signally failed in this) was difficult, and required hours of study; yet a Chinese scholar, who, you knew little about teaching! On one occasion Mr. Pierce discouraged to the extent that he was not able to see how he could continue his work. His wife, however, took a brighter view of the matter, and she encouraged him as best she could. He again turned to the Bible, and on his knees he sought the Lord to enable them to learn the language that they might give the story of Life to those who knew Him not. God graciously answered that prayer, and he became an accomplished Chinese scholar, and could speak and write the language without difficulty.

He was tireless in his efforts to give the Gospel to the people. He visited all the neighboring villages, and their adjacent country-sides, in towns and villages with a pen of seven thousand square miles of territory in and around Yangchow.
